record.paper_title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
record.original_question: What data are needed to calculate a social-resilience measure? The question should specify how relational, longitudinal, and multivariate information about agents, interactions, signed relations, propensities, and temporal centralities can be used to estimate robustness, adaptivity, and resilience.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a social system modeled as a time-evolving multilayer network in which a set of agents A = {a_1, ..., a_n} interact over time. Assume the following data structures may be observed:

(i) Relational data: a sequence of (possibly signed) interaction graphs G_t = (A, E_t, w_t, s_t), where E_t ⊆ A × A is the set of directed dyadic interactions at time t, w_t : E_t → ℝ_{>0} assigns interaction intensities, and s_t : E_t → {+1, −1} assigns a sign (positive or negative relation).
(ii) Longitudinal data: observations of these graphs at discrete times t = 1, 2, ..., T, allowing reconstruction of trajectories of dyads and of individual agents.
(iii) Multivariate data: attribute vectors x_i(t) ∈ ℝ^d for each agent a_i recording features such as activity, role, or context, plus exogenous shock indicators ξ(t).

From such data, define operational estimators for:
 • the robustness R(t) of the system, intended as its capacity to maintain a reference structural/functional state under perturbations;
 • the adaptivity A(t), intended as its capacity to reorganize interactions in response to perturbations;
 • the resilience Res(t), combining robustness and adaptivity over a recovery window after a shock.

The problem is: determine the minimal sufficient set of relational, longitudinal, and multivariate observables — including signed relations, inferred interaction propensities p_{ij}(t) (probabilities that agents i and j interact), and temporal centrality measures C_i(t) — from which the quantities R(t), A(t), and Res(t) can be consistently estimated for a generic social system. Specify (a) which observables are required, (b) how propensities and temporal centralities are to be inferred from the raw interaction logs, and (c) how the resulting estimates of robustness, adaptivity, and resilience are to be assembled into a single resilience measure.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is conceptual and methodological: it asks what data suffice to compute a general social-resilience measure. No definitive consensus answer or unique solution appears in the literature; resilience quantification in social systems remains an active and open research direction, with proposed but non-canonical frameworks combining temporal networks, signed relations, and inferred propensities.
